# TwoRoom Rule Group And Compromise Summary

## Final Decision

- Main analysis path: use V4 full q with V4 group explanation.
- Main V4 explanation unit: group 0, rules `[15, 2, 8, 11]`.
- White-box sparse reference: keep V4.1/V4.2 as explanatory baselines, not as the main prediction-module input yet.
- V4.2 status: Partial Go as a compromise diagnostic. It achieves the target active-rule range and has strong rule/group ablation, but q_v42+action does not beat q_v41+action on residual MSE, so it should not replace V4 as the main line.
- Best V4.2 model: `v42_tau05_topk6_hard_medium_R16`, active_rule_count = 5.4896.

## Run Provenance Note

The server checkout still reported git commit `4f42a43` because the server could not reliably fast-forward from GitHub. The V5.2/V4.2 scripts were synchronized to the server from the local experiment branch by `scp`; this report commit contains the scripts used for the analysis, including the V5.2 action-alignment fix and the V4.2 `.pt.pt` compatibility fix. No LeWM encoder, predictor, train loop, loss, module, or environment code was modified.

This summary combines V5.2 V4 rule-group validation and V4.2 compromise q diagnostics.

Recommended decision should be made from: V4 group functional evidence, V4.2 performance relative to V4/V4.1, active rule count, and ablation strength.

---

# TwoRoom V5.2 V4 Rule Group Validation

V5.2 validates whether V4 rule groups are useful beyond visualization. It audits all V4 rules, audits co-activation groups, tests group-only performance, and masks groups in a fixed full-q diagnostic head.

## Provisional Judgment

V4 full q remains useful. Group 0 is the main V4 explanatory unit if it keeps high hard enrichment and its mask damage exceeds random. If group-only retention is limited, group 0 should be used as explanation rather than replacement input.

## Answers

- Group 0 is more stable than any one soft rule when interpreted as a co-activation unit.
- Group 0 with rules `[15,2,8,11]` is the current main V4 interpretation unit because it is hard-enriched and high-residual.
- V4 should be explained through groups first, single rules second.

# TwoRoom V4.2 Compromise KANFIS q

V4.2 trains only an external compromise q layer from h. It does not modify LeWM, does not connect to ARPredictor, and does not use q->h reconstruction, h mimicry, hidden distillation, or image reconstruction.

## Judgment Template

V4.2 is Go only if it is closer to V4 performance than V4.1 while improving active rule count and visual clarity. Otherwise, keep V4 full q as main and V4.1/V4.2 as explanatory baselines.


---
